§ IIThe argument

Every matter is argued the same way.

  1. 01

    Intake

    A partner hears the whole story first.

  2. 02

    Analysis

    Two or three points the matter turns on.

  3. 03

    Position

    A written recommendation in plain English.

  4. 04

    Resolution

    Negotiated if possible, tried if necessary.

Memorandum of counselp. 1 of 4

In the matter of your decision

§ 1Statement of facts

You tell us what happened. We listen first, ask for the few documents that matter, and write the facts down before anyone offers an opinion.

Your call is answered by a partner.

§ 2Questions presented

We separate what the law says from what the other side hopes it says, and name the two or three points on which the whole matter will turn.

Usually two or three issues, rarely more.

§ 3Recommended course

You receive a written position: the strongest path, what it will cost, where the risk sits, and the alternatives we rejected and why.

Fixed-fee quote included.

§ 4Disposition

We negotiate first and try the matter if we must. You hear from us the moment the picture changes, and before you have to ask.

A status note every Friday.
